steps.title: Register the Dropbox app and select files.metadata.read
steps.detail: In the App Console, create the app, select the metadata read permission, record the app key and secret server-side, and add the redirect URI.
steps.doneWhen: App exists in the App Console with files.metadata.read selected, an app key stored in a secret manager, and a registered redirect URI.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you’ll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the App Console
. That page will guide you through the process of registering your app, selecting permissions, and obtaining an app key and secret (a.k.a. client_id and client_secret ) and inputting redirect

steps.title: Implement the authorization URL and code-to-token callback
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with response_type=code and the redirect URI. On callback, exchange the code at the token endpoint using the client secret on the server. Store the resulting user token per customer account.
steps.doneWhen: Code builds an authorization URL and a callback handler that exchanges the code for an access token in a test environment.

evidence.quote: Method: GET Example: Auth URL for code flow
Example: code flow access token request

steps.title: Authorize a representative individual test account
steps.detail: Sign in with a test individual Dropbox account (not a team admin) and grant the app access. The callback must return a code and the token exchange must succeed. Boundary check: the consent screen and granted access show only the metadata read permission, and no team scope is requested.
steps.doneWhen: The test individual account completes consent and the callback yields an access token with the metadata read scope only.

steps.doneWhen: The response returns an entries array and has_more or cursor, and the request log contains only list_folder calls.

steps.detail: Pass the returned cursor to list_folder/continue and repeat while has_more is true. Boundary check: confirm each page is metadata only and the loop stops when has_more is false.
steps.doneWhen: Continuation returns further entries and the loop ends with has_more false.
